name: level-ldtk
description: Import LDtk-exported levels (tiles + entities) into the spawn pipeline
postInstallNotes:
## level-ldtk installed

Export your LDtk project to a `.ldtk` file under `Content/`, then add it to your `.mgcb`:
```
#begin Levels/your_project.ldtk
/importer:LDtkImporter
/processor:LDtkProcessor
/build:Levels/your_project.ldtk
```

Reference the LDtkMonogame content pipeline DLL in your csproj's `MonoGameMGCBAdditionalArguments`:
```
<MonoGameMGCBAdditionalArguments>$(MonoGameMGCBAdditionalArguments) /reference:$(NuGetPackageRoot)ldtkmonogame.contentpipeline/1.8.0/lib/net8.0/LDtk.ContentPipeline.dll</MonoGameMGCBAdditionalArguments>
```

At runtime, compose this module's own loader **instead of** `level-loading`'s native-only `LevelLoadRequestSystem` (both subscribe to `LoadLevelRequest`), then the parsers, then `EntitySpawnSystem`:
```csharp
new LDtkLevelLoadSystem(world, content)   // LoadLevelRequest → LDtkLevelDataComponent
new LDtkTileParserSystem(world, content, ...)
new LDtkEntityParserSystem(world, ...)
```

The parsers subscribe to `LDtkLevelDataComponent` being added (this module's own world singleton, holding the full `LDtkLevel`) — `level-loading` carries no LDtk type.

In your factories, layer-derived data now arrives on the `ldtk:` `CustomFields` channel instead of the removed `request.Layer` — read it defensively, since a code-driven spawn carries no `ldtk:` keys:
```csharp
var opacity  = request.CustomFields.TryGetValue(LDtkSpawnFields.LayerOpacity, out var o) && o is float f ? f : 1f;
var gridSize = request.CustomFields.TryGetValue(LDtkSpawnFields.GridSize, out var g) && g is int i ? i : 16;
```

**Premises:** `docs/premises.md`
